{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, the passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same story.","text":"Mara held her breath. “What happens when it ends?”

The child’s voice came from the little window. “I get to go home.”

Finn started down the stairs, but the lantern flame shivered. Mara caught his sleeve. “Wait.”

Her grandmother’s warning pressed against her thoughts: Not every way home leads to the same place.

“Who are you?” Mara called.

A pause. Then: “I’m you.”

The tune hummed again, and the stone steps trembled beneath their feet. In the window, a small face appeared—Mara’s own face, younger by years, with mud on its cheeks and a silver key clutched in one fist.

Finn stared. “That can’t be.”

The other Mara pressed her palm to the glass. “You brought the story this far. You have to finish it.”

“What story?”

“The one about the valley forgetting.” Her reflection glanced over its shoulder. Behind it, the window showed a place Mara recognized: her village, its roofs buried under snow, its lamps all dark. “When the last name disappears, no one remembers the way back.”

From above, her grandmother called, “Mara, come back!” Her voice sounded distant now, as though the stairs were stretching longer with every breath.

Mara looked at the silver key. “How do I open the window?”

“You don’t,” said the child. “You tell me the part I don’t know.”

The lantern flared. The tune rose into a question, and Mara understood: the story wasn’t waiting for an ending. It was waiting for her to remember what came next.

She began to speak."}
